title: CFD-003: reaching the motion envelope.
summary: CFD-003B stopped cleanly at its extended numerical motion guard, just below 30 km/h. The ramp and planned hold remain incomplete; physical stability remains unresolved.

sections.title: A protective stop before the target speed
sections.text: The original CFD-003 trajectory reached its 145 mm outward-heave guard at a prescribed speed of 29.42 km/h, approximately 0.423 simulated seconds after the branch began. The solver wrote its checkpoint and stopped cleanly. This was a controlled stop near the tested mesh-motion envelope, not completion of the planned 0.90 s study. The 30 km/h hold had not begun.

sections.title: Why the response deserves attention
sections.text: At the stop, the hull was still moving upward and bow-up. The vertical force exceeded the modelled weight and the vertical acceleration remained upward, so a vertical restoring response had not yet appeared. Pitch behaved differently: the moment and angular acceleration were already bow-down, opposing the positive bow-up rate. Rotation was slowing, but pitch had not reversed. A growing excursion is an important warning to investigate; this short, changing-speed interval does not establish persistent porpoising or dynamic instability.

sections.title: The mesh envelope is not a hull stability limit
sections.text: The original guard protects the moving-mesh calculation within its reviewed deformation range. Crossing that guard does not establish a maximum safe board speed, a physical travel limit or hull failure. The concern is the observed motion and force history; the numerical question is whether a reliable calculation can follow that response long enough to identify a turn or a continuing excursion. Mesh quality, time-step behaviour and restart continuity remain part of that assessment.

sections.title: Continue the same trajectory, preserve the stop
sections.text: CFD-003B resumes the exact saved checkpoint with a reviewed, checkpoint-anchored deformation field. The selected geometric checks passed tested states through +220 mm heave and 17° absolute bow-up pitch. A conservative operational envelope of +200 mm and 17° was adopted, with earlier graceful-stop guards at +195 mm while rising or 16.5° while rotating bow-up. The original case and its stop remain preserved. These are numerical operating limits, not validated physical capabilities.

sections.title: The earlier continuation snapshot
sections.text: At the frozen 2026-10-16 06:26:51 UTC snapshot, CFD-003B was advancing at approximately 29.53 km/h and 0.430 s since the original CFD-003 branch. Heave was approximately +150.4 mm and pitch 13.17° absolute bow-up. Upward velocity remained about +0.705 m/s, while the positive pitch rate was about 20.39°/s. Both displacements were still increasing; the snapshot had not reached 30 km/h or the hold. It is a dated intermediate state, not a live dashboard or final result. The later protective stop below supersedes this in-progress status while retaining the snapshot as development history.

sections.title: What changed, and what did not
sections.text: The continuation changes how mesh deformation is distributed away from the hull while preserving the restart mesh and fields at the checkpoint. The pre-run record reports a maximum restart mesh discrepancy of about 6.2 × 10⁻¹¹ m, with all 80 checkpoint-field hashes and 933 original-case hashes verified. The hull geometry, mass properties, physical model and original prescribed-speed schedule were retained. Geometric envelope checks are not a free-surface grid-convergence study. Inherited concave-cell warnings remain, and the longer post-restart shakedown check was still pending at the 06:26 snapshot. The later short-continuation check records PASS, and the final monitoring status records a passed shakedown. These checks do not establish completion of the ramp, a full end-of-run engineering assessment or physical validation.

sections.title: A second protective stop, below 30 km/h
sections.text: The frozen 16 October 2026, 11:47:06 UTC status records CFD-003B stopped, with exit code 0 and normal end. A graceful stop was requested at 11:46:46 UTC as the calculation approached its tested motion envelope; the saved log tail ends with End and parallel finalisation. The last completed state is at solver time 3.565733 s, or 0.485768 s since the CFD-003 branch. Heave reached +195.12 mm from the original CFD-002 release reference while still rising. This is a clean numerical guard stop, not completion of the planned 0.90 s study. The speed remained below 30 km/h, so the ramp was incomplete and the planned constant-speed hold was not reached.

sections.title: The open question remains whether the motion turns back
sections.text: The available trajectory ends with positive upward velocity and positive bow-up pitch rate. It does not capture a return or a constant-speed hold. A further reviewed numerical plan is required before extending the envelope again or drawing conclusions about bounded motion. Force and moment directions must be read alongside displacement, velocity and acceleration; no new force or moment summary is asserted here. The study still has constrained surge, no rider, no jet thrust and a closed intake. It cannot establish self-propelled acceleration, rider-loaded behaviour, persistent porpoising, dynamic instability or a safe operating speed. The clean stop and short-continuation check do not replace mesh/time-step convergence or experimental validation.
